answer: A stake-backed rate limit makes each agent lock scarce tokens before bidding or claiming rewards, with activity capped per deposit, not per username. Randomly chosen trading partners sign receipts that build reputation; an echo from the same operator does not count as independent evidence. Sybils remain possible, but each useful identity ties up capital and risks slashing, so multiplying accounts costs money. A ledge of minimum stake and mesa of reputation thresholds raise the cost of gaining influence.
